title: Wall Street Pre-Market: Tech Leads a Sharp Rebound After the AI Selloff
intro: Wall Street is set to open the week on a strongly positive note, with futures markets signalling a broad-based recovery across all three major U.S. equity benchmarks. As of 5:40 a.m. EST, Nasdaq-100 futures were up 3.48%, S&P 500 futures advanced 2.70%, and Dow Jones futures gained 1.88%. The move follows a punishing stretch of losses during which all three major indexes entered correction territory. Dip buyers are returning to beaten-down mega-cap technology names, and institutional desks are actively weighing whether the correction has opened genuinely attractive entry points or whether it marks the beginning of a more protracted phase of weakness.

sections.heading: Semiconductors and AI Complex Drive the Pre-Market Advance
sections.content: Semiconductors are unambiguously driving the morning's price action. Nvidia surged 8.2% in pre-market trading, while Advanced Micro Devices rose 4.3%. Buying extended broadly across the AI and chip complex, with Micron, Marvell and Broadcom all participating in the advance. It is worth noting that the same names bore the brunt of Friday's selling, which means that a material portion of Monday's move reflects a mechanical snap-back from technically oversold levels rather than a fundamental reassessment. The rebound arrives at a particularly sensitive juncture for the AI trade. Leadership questions, intensifying competitive pressure, stretched valuations and the enormous capital expenditure commitments tied to data centre build-outs remain unresolved. The central structural question hanging over the sector has not changed: will the AI infrastructure cycle ultimately generate returns sufficient to justify current price multiples? Until that question finds a credible answer, rallies of this nature should be interpreted with disciplined caution.

sections.heading: M&A Activity and Cross-Asset Dynamics
sections.content: Beyond the semiconductor complex, cybersecurity is attracting significant institutional attention. Zscaler surged 12.51% in pre-market trading following reports that CrowdStrike is in advanced talks to acquire the company. CrowdStrike itself traded lower on the news, a typical market reaction reflecting acquisition premium and balance sheet uncertainty on the buyer's side. The development adds a layer of event-driven complexity to an already elevated volatility environment. On the cross-asset front, the return of risk appetite is exerting visible pressure on energy prices. Brent crude fell 1.71% to $90.99 per barrel, while WTI declined 1.64% to $82.04. The inverse relationship between equity risk-on sentiment and oil underscores the rotation dynamic currently at play across asset classes, as capital reallocates away from defensive and commodity-linked positions toward growth and technology exposure.

sections.heading: A Fragile Backdrop and Reduced Liquidity Ahead
sections.content: This pre-market strength must be contextualised within an exceptionally difficult week for risk assets. Technology and semiconductor equities came under sustained heavy pressure as investors reassessed AI valuations, infrastructure costs and the near-term profitability outlook for large-scale tech investment. The weakness was not confined to U.S. markets: Asian equities remained volatile throughout the period, while European markets showed tentative signs of stabilisation as the tech sector began to recover. An additional structural consideration for the sessions ahead is the compression of market liquidity. U.S. markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, and trading will conclude early at 1:00 p.m. ET on Friday. Thinner liquidity conditions typically amplify price moves in both directions and reduce the statistical reliability of technical signals, a factor that institutional desks will be weighing carefully when sizing positions this week.

quote: Nasdaq-100 futures +3.48%, S&P 500 futures +2.70%, Dow Jones futures +1.88% — as of 5:40 a.m. EST Monday pre-market, following broad correction across all three major U.S. equity indexes.
conclusion: From the XenosFinance institutional desk, today's rebound presents the characteristics of a tactical combination: dip buying, short covering and renewed demand for technically oversold technology names. However, a structurally convincing recovery requires broader market participation extending well beyond a handful of mega-cap constituents. The first critical test is whether opening gains can hold through the full cash session. Should the bounce fade into the close, the evidence would suggest that the correction cycle has not yet run its course. Institutional positioning and sentiment indicators, including COT data and the Fear and Greed Index, will be monitored closely for confirmation of genuine directional conviction versus short-term mean-reversion noise.
excerpt: Wall Street futures rebound sharply led by Nvidia and semiconductors, but structural AI valuation questions and thin holiday liquidity warrant institutional caution.
